title: dot11decrypt: Cleanup debug log level usage
description:
The debug log levels used in dot11decrypt are pretty much random.
Cleanup how the different levels are used and at the same time change
to standard wslog log levels.

With this change log levels are used as follows:

WARNING - Allocation failures or unexpected (but handled) errors.
DEBUG - Debug messages mainly related to key derivation.
NOISY - Debug messages related to packet decryption.

NOTE: Debug messages are compile time disabled by default just as
before.

Change-Id: Ie33252a8b49488d5e56312bad964850c18ec1a1a

notes.body: This will result in compilation errors with -DDISABLE_DEBUG=True (macro redefinition).

Thanks. Would it be OK to just protect it with ifndef or should we skip compile time disabling completely for these logs? There are plenty of per packet prints under noisy tag. Not sure if it has any noticable performance impact as long as the logs are runtime disabled.

I am in favor of **not** disabling with `#ifdef`. First that way the logging doesn't require recompilation, that's already a plus. Then the reasons are the same as arguments against dead code, over time it might bit rot. The performance issue is already covered with `-DDISABLE_DEBUG=True` or `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release` I think (and as you say it might not even be noticeable).

The only reason to disable it at compile time would be to bring down the excessive verbosity for the common use case, but I think that is also covered by having "debug" and "noisy".

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/3393/diffs?diff_id=203331749&start_sha=78e5e31314f9a36c8becfac2ce5e322e72827549#2c24c129343774cef996ac95face57b1b0ad4774_13_13)

Ok, so I decided to remove this #define WS_DISABLE_DEBUG line and have the logs built in after running some simple performance measurements with and without this patch. Measured the time it took for tshark to decrypt an 802.11 sniffer log with ~800k encrypted data frames (iperf packets) and didn't notice any performance penalty. Time variations running tshark multiple times were larger than difference seen with / without this patch.
Can you remove the old Change-Id for Gerrit from the commit message?
Ah sorry for that. Yes I will.
